A metahuman who can pass for human: human NPCs start Neutral and skip the Racism Table unless up close. Elves, dwarfs and orks only; not metavariants.
items.s: Elves, dwarfs and orks only; not metavariants. Edge · Social

items.efd: −1 target number per point (1–2) on Social Skill Tests; people tend to trust and respect you.
Each point gives 2 bonus Force Points to spend as you like, up to 6 Force Points in all.

For magicians: you can sustain up to Intelligence + 1 spells at once, and the book gives a +1 target modifier when casting sustained spells. Check with your GM how this sits with the normal sustaining penalty.
+1 die per point (1–4) on Spell Resistance Tests. You can’t be magically active, and it resists helpful spells like Heal too.
Innate ability to cast one Combat spell at Force = starting Magic − 1 (raise it with spell foci or initiation). Needs a Magic Rating of 1 or more.
Innate ability to cast one Detection spell at Force = starting Magic − 1. Needs a Magic Rating of 1 or more.
Innate ability to cast one Health spell at Force = starting Magic − 1. Needs a Magic Rating of 1 or more.
Innate ability to cast one Illusion spell at Force = starting Magic − 1. Needs a Magic Rating of 1 or more.
Innate ability to cast one Manipulation spell at Force = starting Magic − 1. Needs a Magic Rating of 1 or more.
Summon one kind of spirit without the Conjuring Skill: watchers (3 points) or one type of elemental or nature spirit (5 points). One spirit at a time. Needs a Magic Rating of 1 or more.
Astral perception without being a full magician; no astral projection or other magical skills. Can learn Aura Reading (Awakenings p. 96). Needs a Magic Rating of 1 or more.
+2 to the Link Test of any ritual sorcery aimed at you, which also hurts friendly rituals trying to find or help you.
Legal permits for restricted foci and Class C cyberware in your country. Needs a valid SIN. Other runners may get suspicious, and the authorities can revoke the permits.

Access to top-end implants: 2 points for Availability 10 and alphaware, 4 for Availability 20, cultured bioware and betaware, 6 for deltaware of any Availability. Prices don’t change. Easy to unbalance a game; GM’s call.
+1 target number for every test with one chosen skill (one you know or can default to). Once per skill.

Allergic to a substance or condition. Value = how common it is (Uncommon −1, Common −2) plus the reaction (Mild −1: +1 to tests while exposed; Moderate −2: weapons of it get +2 Power; Severe −3: a Light wound per minute of exposure).
Your body rejects all cyberware and bioware; replacements must be cloned from your own cells. −2 instead of −5 for magicians and adepts. Not with Sensitive System.
items.s: −2 for magically active characters. Flaw · Physical

items.efd: +6 target number on anything that needs sight. −2 instead of −6 for magically active characters.
items.s: −2 for magically active characters. Flaw · Physical

items.efd: You’ll die soon: the GM secretly rolls 3D6 for the number of game months left. The GM may later let you swap it for other Flaws worth −6.
+4 target number when telling colors apart matters. Neural, so cybereyes don’t fix it. Not with Blind.
No Hearing Tests, and +4 on tests where hearing matters (such as Surprise). Cyberware can’t cure it.
Each point (−1 to −5) lowers the racial maximum of your Physical Attributes by 1.
Count your wounds one level worse when working out wound modifiers.
+6 extra on visual tests in Full Darkness or Minimal Light. Not with Blind.
Paralyzed from the waist down; moves by wheelchair and halves Combat Pools. Can’t be fixed with cyberware. Not with Quadriplegic.
Paralyzed from the neck down: no physical tasks, needs a Hospitalized lifestyle and helpers. No effect in the Matrix or astral space. Can’t be cured. Not with Paraplegic.

Cyberware Essence costs are doubled and bioware Body Index doubled (not cultured or self-cloned parts). −2 for magically active characters, who also lose the extra Essence from Magic. Not with Bio-Rejection.
items.s: −2 for magically active characters. Flaw · Physical

items.efd: −1 Body die when resisting disease (never below 1 die). Often follows heavy cyberware or bioware surgery.
Memory loss, −2 to −5: at −2 you don’t know who you are but keep your skills; at −5 you don’t know your own skills or Attributes either, and the GM keeps the sheet.
Irrationally vicious in a fight: it takes at least 3 Combat Turns to break away (each success on a Willpower (6) Test cuts 1, minimum 1) unless every opponent is down. Not with Combat Paralysis.
You freeze: your first Initiative roll in any combat (physical, astral or Matrix) counts as the lowest possible, and +2 on Surprise Tests. Not with Combat Monster.
A compulsion you can’t control. Worth more the more trouble it causes, from −1 (compulsively tidy) to about −3 (compulsively cracking corporate hosts).
A set trigger can bring on vivid flashbacks: make a Willpower (6) Test or be helpless for 1D6 minutes. Agree the trigger with the GM.
When danger shows up you must pass a Willpower (4) Test or jump straight in without thinking.
Can’t read: most Technical and Knowledge Skills are out, +4 on computer tests and no Computer Skill above 1. Not with any Education Edge; can become Uneducated through roleplay.
+1 target number on all Perception Tests, astral included. No effect on combat vision or range modifiers.
Won’t kill except in self-defense, and then as humanely as possible; no planned killings, and you push your team not to kill. Not with Total Pacifist.
A deep fear of a trigger. Value = trigger (Uncommon −1, Common −2) plus reaction (Mild −1: +1 to tests; Moderate −2: +2; Severe −3). The table on p. 35 lists −1 to −4.
Can’t kill anything smarter than an insect (insect spirits included), whatever the provocation; if you do, 2D6 weeks of depression. Not with Pacifist.

Only basic reading, writing and arithmetic: no Knowledge or Technical Skills at creation, and +1 for each dot when defaulting on the Skill Web. Can become High School or Technical School Education through roleplay.
You must avenge every slight, in proportion: a threat or a punch for an insult, often death for an injury. You carry grudges until settled.

Hooked on a drug, BTLs or similar; withdrawal after a few hours without. Strongly Addictive: Willpower (6) Test to resist, +1 per day without. Debilitating: +2 to tests while high. Incapacitating: helpless while high. This page lists −1, −2 and −3; the p. 35 table lists −1, −1 and −2. Kicking it costs 10 × its value in Karma.
items.s: Strongly addictive −1, debilitating −1, incapacitating −2. Flaw · Social

items.efd: A real job besides running: time and responsibilities, but also cover, legit contacts and pay (−1: 1,000¥, −2: 2,500¥, −3: 5,000¥+ a month). The p. 35 table lists it as an Edge; its description makes it a Flaw.
items.s: A real job besides running; the p. 35 table lists it as an Edge, but its description (p. 31) makes it a Flaw. Flaw · Social

items.efd: A flashy look or manner everyone remembers, which makes you dangerously easy to recall.
items.s: People easily remember you. Flaw · Social

items.efd: A human who wants to be an elf: +2 to understand or speak Sperethiel and +2 on Social Skill Tests with elves. Surgery can let you pass, but elves who find out turn Hostile. Humans only.
−1 point per extra enemy taken at creation (Enemies, p. 71).
+1 target number per point (up to −4) on all Social Skill Tests; people react badly to you.
A terrible secret. Every two or three sessions the GM threatens to expose it. If it comes out, it may turn into Bad Reputation.
Someone who relies on you for time and money, such as a child, parent or old friend. The GM sets the value.
For a reason the GM picks, your contacts stop talking to you. Resolve it through roleplay, maybe a whole campaign.
No social graces: +2 on Social Skill Tests, Negotiation and Etiquette included.
You gain a Karma Pool point for every 20 Good Karma instead of every 10.
Someone planted a cortex or cranial bomb in your head (Cybertechnology p. 27), free of charge. The GM decides who and what they want. If you disarm it, the GM may swap in other Flaws of equal value.
Your Enemies actively hunt you, and a new one replaces any you kill. −2: a Rank 3 Enemy (or +1 to one); −4: Rank 4 (or +2); −6: Rank 5–6 with GM approval (or +3).
An implant you don’t know about, chosen by the GM, that shows up when the GM decides: kicking in at a bad moment or setting off a scanner.

Contacts must be street level, corp security and Lone Star have your face and file, Lone Star harasses you on sight, you can never get a legal SIN, and you report to a parole officer who can kick in your door.
